summary_paragraph: A male patient was admitted with chest pain and pink-tinged sputum, found to have a large endophytic thrombus in the proximal descending aorta on CT angiography. Despite being on Lovenox for Factor V Leiden, he developed this arterial clot, likely due to multiple cardiovascular risk factors including smoking, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. He was managed medically with a heparin drip, which was briefly held after a minor episode of hemoptysis but then resumed. Hematology and pulmonology were consulted; no additional clotting disorders were immediately identified, and the hemoptysis was attributed to bronchitis and anticoagulation. Pain was managed with Neurontin, Lidoderm patches, and Dilaudid. By the third hospital day, his pain was controlled, and he was stable for discharge. He was transitioned to home on Lovenox, with follow-up planned in hematology, primary care, and for repeat imaging. Discharge instructions emphasized smoking cessation, activity restrictions, and medication adherence.
problems: Embolism and thrombosis of thoracic aorta
